title: Tunisian smock stitch cowl
excerpt: A textured cowl in aran yarn worked in Tunisian smocking stitch. Gathered columns give the finished piece a honeyed, gathered look similar to traditional smocked fabric.
sourceNotes: Tunisian smock stitch combines standard Tunisian simple stitch with post-stitch gathering, a technique that has grown in popularity through Tunisian crochet communities.

glossaryTerms.definition: A Tunisian technique where a post-stitch is worked around two vertical bars several rows below the current row, pulling those bars together to create a gathered effect.
Working Tunisian crochet in a continuous tube using two balls of yarn and two hooks, or a long circular hook. Avoids seaming for cowls and sleeves.
The upright strand at the front of each Tunisian stitch. It is the main insertion point for all Tunisian stitches.
A post stitch worked around two vertical bars at once, several rows below. It cinches the fabric and creates the smocked column.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 sts x 12 rows = 10 x 10 cm in Tunisian simple stitch with aran yarn.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Approx. 56 cm circumference x 30 cm tall.

Smocking row: work 4 rows of Tunisian simple stitch, then on the smocking row insert the hook around the vertical bar of the stitch 4 rows below, insert again around the next vertical bar, and pull both loops onto the hook. Continue across. Repeat the 4-row set throughout.
Join 78 ch into a ring with a slip stitch. Work 3 rows of Tunisian simple stitch in the round to establish the base.
Rows 1 to 4: Tunisian simple stitch. Row 5 (smocking row): work gathering posts around pairs of vertical bars 4 rows below across all stitches. Repeat these 5 rows until the cowl measures 30 cm.
Work a slip stitch bind-off round through each vertical bar. Fasten off. Weave in all ends with the tapestry needle.
